Notes: The paper's main result is that the jackknife correction reduces selection bias in the winning arm's estimate. The bias is Theta(K^{-1/2}) without correction only when the leading coefficient c_1 is nonzero; after correction it is o(K^{-1/2}) under Assumptions 1-2 with positive gaps between arm means. A secondary result, in Section 6, shows that when gaps shrink at the K^{-1/2} rate no estimator removes the first-order bias uniformly.
Draft: Under Assumptions 1-2 with arm means separated by positive gaps, we show that the jackknife removes the leading K^{-1/2} term at every fixed configuration. Where c_1 is nonzero, the expected bias magnitude falls from Theta(K^{-1/2}) to o(K^{-1/2}). For gaps shrinking at the K^{-1/2} rate, we characterize first-order residuals and prove that no estimator removes first-order bias uniformly.
